style.summary:
style of A: A is brief and questioning, asking a yes-or-no question and acknowledging with O_K.
style of B: B is casual and short, answering Yeah, sure and trailing off with a partial sentence.

A: A's questions set the topic and make B answer, which gives A the lead.
A's O_K closes each answer, so A decides when a point is finished.
A's brevity keeps the tone efficient and in A's control.
B: B's casual Yeah, sure gives B an easygoing tone that puts A at ease.
B's partial answer leaves room for B to add or shape the account.
B's willingness to answer quickly shows B is open and cooperative.

A: Questions set the topic only if B answers them, and B's reply decides what the topic becomes.
Closing an answer with O_K shows A accepting B's answer, so B's account is what gets closed.
Efficiency is A's style, but it depends on B supplying the information.
B: An easygoing tone is passive, and A's questions are what keep the exchange going.
A partial answer lets B shape the account only if A allows B to finish, and A's O_K shows A is ready to move on.
Being cooperative means answering A's questions, which leaves A setting the terms.

content.summary:
content of A: A asks whether Hari was on the phone.
content of B: B confirms that Hari was on the phone and begins to describe the meeting as a discussion between Hari and someone else.

A: A's question sets the factual point that the exchange turns on.
A's question about who was present makes A the one who sets the detail.
A's question determines what B must explain.
B: B has the information about the meeting, which makes B the source of the content.
B's description of the discussion gives B the framing of what happened.
B's partial answer starts the account that B will complete.

A: A factual point is set by A's question, but B's answer determines what the point is.
Setting the detail is A's, but the content of the answer is B's to give.
What B must explain is shaped by B, who decides how much to say.
B: Having information is useful only if B shares it, and A's question controls whether B does.
Framing the discussion is B's, but A's question about the phone is what makes it relevant.
An account that B starts can be stopped by A's next question.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A asks, receives the answer, and moves on with O_K.
coordination of B: B answers and then begins a longer account that is left unfinished.

A: A's questions keep the exchange moving and set each step.
A's O_K closes the turn and passes the exchange on.
A decides when the topic moves on.
B: B's account gives B a longer turn, which holds the floor.
B's unfinished sentence leaves the next part of the turn to B.
B's answers are short enough that A has to respond to them.

A: Moving the exchange on depends on B's answers, which give A the next step to take.
Closing a turn with O_K is an acknowledgment, and B's account continues after it.
Deciding when to move on is A's, but B can keep going when A pauses.
B: A longer turn is held only while A allows it, and A's O_K shows A is ready to take over.
An unfinished sentence can be cut off by A, which means A decides whether B finishes.
Short answers mean B is not controlling the exchange, since A's questions define each answer.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A is polite and attentive, asking about the participants.
engagement of B: B is informal and willing, answering and beginning to explain.

A: A's question about who was on the call shows attention to the detail of the meeting.
A's acknowledgments show A is following the account.
A's questions keep A involved in the exchange.
B: B's readiness to explain shows B is involved in the meeting.
B's easy answers show B's willingness to share.
B's account shows B has knowledge of the discussion.

A: Attention to the detail is A's, and B is the one who has the knowledge to answer it.
Following the account is passive, and B's description is what A is following.
Being involved depends on B's answers, which A cannot give.
B: Involvement in the meeting is B's, but A's question shows A wants to know the details that B has.
Willingness to share depends on A asking, so A decides what B shares.
Knowledge is B's, but A's questions decide which part of it comes out.
